quizzes.title: India-UAE Partnership: Trade and Energy
quizzes.passage: India and the United Arab Emirates have widened their partnership well beyond trade in goods. During a visit to India by the UAE President, the two governments agreed on a target to expand bilateral commerce over the coming years and promised to create new trade corridors and digital platforms to support it. Energy is another pillar of the relationship, and an agreement between an Emirati gas company and an Indian refiner will supply liquefied natural gas under a supply deal. The two sides also agreed to explore cooperation in advanced nuclear technologies, including small modular reactors and nuclear safety frameworks, a step that follows India's recent law enabling wider international nuclear collaboration. Security ties are growing as well, with a framework for cooperation in defence technology, military training, cyber and emerging security domains. Digital policy is part of the agenda too: a proposal would allow a country to store its most important national data in offshore digital infrastructure, protecting it from cyberattacks, natural disasters and geopolitical disruption. The initiatives deepen economic and strategic ties between the two countries. The agreements cover several sectors at once. Taken together, these steps show that the partnership now covers commerce, energy, nuclear technology, defence and digital infrastructure.

questions.q: By what year did India and the UAE agree to double their bilateral trade to over USD 200 billion?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the two countries agreed to double bilateral trade to over USD 200 billion by 2032.

questions.q: In 2022, the UAE signed its Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement first with which country?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that India became the first country with which the UAE signed a CEPA in 2022.

questions.q: According to the booklet, what share of India's remittance flows did the UAE account for?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the UAE accounted for 18% of India's remittance flows.

questions.q:
Read the statements and choose the correct option.
Assertion (A): ADNOC Gas's LNG supply agreement with HPCL is a short-term arrangement.
Reason (R): ADNOC Gas agreed to supply LNG to HPCL for 10 years.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.explanation: The booklet describes a 10-year LNG supply, so A is false while R is true.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Desert Cyclone   ->   A. Air Defence Force
II. Zayed Talwar   ->   B. Military
III. Desert Eagle   ->   C. Abu Dhabi
IV. BAPS Hindu Temple   ->   D. Naval
questions.explanation: Desert Cyclone is the military, Zayed Talwar the naval, Desert Eagle the Air Defence Force, and the BAPS temple is in Abu Dhabi.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. ADNOC Gas agreed to supply 0.5 million tonnes per annum of LNG to HPCL for 10 years.
II. Bilateral trade between India and the UAE was US$ 200 billion in FY 2024-25.
III. Estonia launched the world's first data embassy in Luxembourg in 2017.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because bilateral trade was US$ 100 billion in FY 2024-25, while I and III match the booklet.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. India has access to the UAE's Al Dhafra Air Base for refuelling.
2. Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan is the Prime Minister of the UAE.
3. A supercomputing cluster is to be set up under India's AI India Mission as part of the cooperation.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 match the booklet, while statement 2 is wrong because the Prime Minister is Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum.

quizzes.title: India-UAE Ties Beyond Trade
quizzes.passage: The partnership between India and the United Arab Emirates now extends across trade, energy, defence, nuclear technology and digital policy. Both governments have agreed to create new trade corridors and platforms to support commerce. Remittances sent home by workers from the Emirates are an important part of the financial relationship. In energy, an Emirati gas company has signed a supply agreement with an Indian refiner. Military cooperation is also growing, with plans for joint training and work on defence technology. The two sides have also agreed to cooperate in emerging security domains. Scientific cooperation is part of the agenda as well, including a joint project in artificial intelligence and high-performance computing. Cultural ties are visible in a traditional Hindu stone temple in Abu Dhabi, the first of its kind in the UAE. India has also passed a recent law that opens the way for wider international nuclear collaboration. Digital cooperation is also being explored, including a proposal to store critical national data offshore. The UAE's President visited India recently, and the agreements were announced during that visit. The initiatives promote new trade corridors and platforms. Energy, defence and digital policy are being developed in parallel. Taken together, these steps widen the relationship beyond traditional trade.

questions.q: What was India-UAE bilateral trade in FY 2024-25, in US$ billion?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives bilateral trade of US$ 100 billion in FY 2024-25.

questions.q: Which UAE air base has India been given access to for refuelling? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says India has access to the UAE's Al Dhafra Air Base for refuelling.

questions.q: Which Indian law enacted in 2025 enables broader international nuclear collaboration? (name of the Act)
questions.explanation: The booklet links the nuclear cooperation to India's enactment of the SHANTI Act 2025.

questions.q: Under which Indian mission will a supercomputing cluster be set up as part of India-UAE cooperation? (name of mission)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the supercomputing cluster is set up under India's AI India Mission.

questions.q: What is the name of the UAE's first traditional Hindu stone temple, located in Abu Dhabi? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the BAPS Hindu Temple as the UAE's first traditional Hindu stone temple, in Abu Dhabi.

questions.q: For how many years is the ADNOC Gas LNG supply agreement with HPCL? (number of years)
questions.explanation: ADNOC Gas signed a supply agreement with HPCL for 10 years, as stated in the booklet.

questions.q: In which year did Estonia launch the world's first data embassy? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Estonia launched the world's first data embassy in Luxembourg in 2017.

quizzes.title: The UAE and Its Migrant Workers
quizzes.passage: The United Arab Emirates is a federal elective monarchy on the south-eastern side of the Arabian Peninsula. Its government is led by a Prime Minister, Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, and its leadership also includes a President. The UAE has migrant workers whose employment is regulated by a particular system. Their working lives are governed by an arrangement whose name comes from Arabic, and which is used in several Gulf countries. The arrangement can lead to exploitation and poor working conditions. The UAE's coastline meets the waters of the Gulf, and its maritime frontier is shared with other states. The country also operates a nuclear power plant. In trade, the UAE has signed a comprehensive economic partnership with India, and the two countries have agreed to expand cooperation in defence and nuclear technology. The UAE has also had military personnel in Yemen, where it has been part of the anti-Houthi coalition. The UAE's relations with its neighbours have been tested by recent events in Yemen, where the coalition has faced divisions. The UAE has a traditional Hindu stone temple in its capital city. Remittances from the UAE to India are an important part of the financial links between the two countries.

questions.q: Who is the President of the UAE?
questions.explanation: The booklet names Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan as President and Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum as Prime Minister.

questions.q: Which two countries share land borders with the UAE?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the UAE shares land borders with Oman and Saudi Arabia.

questions.q: Under Kafala, which party typically controls a migrant worker's visa and legal status?
options: The in-country sponsor, typically the employer
questions.explanation: Under Kafala, the in-country sponsor, typically the employer, controls the worker's visa and legal status.

questions.q:
Read the statements and choose the correct option.
Assertion (A): Kafala can restrict the freedom of movement of migrant workers.
Reason (R): Under Kafala, workers cannot leave the country without the sponsor's permission.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Because workers need the sponsor's permission to leave, the restriction in R explains the restricted movement named in A.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Kafala   ->   A. Capital of the UAE
II. Barakah   ->   B. Currency of the UAE
III. Abu Dhabi   ->   C. Sponsorship in Arabic
IV. Dirham   ->   D. Arab world's first nuclear power plant
questions.explanation: Kafala means sponsorship in Arabic, Barakah is the Arab world's first nuclear power plant, Abu Dhabi is the capital, and the dirham is the currency.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The UAE's maritime borders in the Persian Gulf are shared with Qatar and Iran.
II. The UAE is a federal elective monarchy of seven emirates.
III. Under Kafala, workers can change jobs without the sponsor's permission.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III is wrong because Kafala workers cannot change jobs without the sponsor's permission.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The UAE's capital is Dubai.
2. Kafala can lead to non-payment of wages for workers.
3. The UAE's currency is the riyal.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement 2 matches the booklet, since the capital is Abu Dhabi and the currency is the dirham.

quizzes.title: UAE Profile and Labour Rules
quizzes.passage: The United Arab Emirates is a federal elective monarchy on the south-eastern side of the Arabian Peninsula. Its territory is organised as a federation of member emirates, and its government is led by a President and a Prime Minister. The country has a coastline on the Gulf, and its maritime boundaries are shared with other states across these waters. Its land borders are with two neighbouring countries on the peninsula. Many migrant workers live in the country, and their presence is regulated by a system in which a party inside the country holds considerable control over the worker's legal status. The arrangement can lead to exploitation, non-payment of wages, poor working conditions and restricted movement. The country operates a nuclear power plant, and it is the first of its kind in the Arab world. In trade, the UAE has a comprehensive economic partnership with India, and remittances from the UAE are an important source of funds for families in India. The two countries have also agreed to cooperate in defence and in nuclear safety. Cultural ties include a traditional Hindu stone temple in the capital city. The UAE's President has visited India recently. The UAE has ties with several neighbours in the Gulf region, and its relations with them have been tested by recent events in Yemen.

questions.q: How many emirates make up the UAE? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the UAE is a federal elective monarchy composed of 7 emirates.

questions.q: What is the capital city of the UAE? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Abu Dhabi as the UAE's capital.

questions.q: What is the currency of the UAE? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the dirham as the UAE's currency.

questions.q: Which Arabic word, meaning 'sponsorship', names the system that places migrant workers under an in-country sponsor? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Kafala means sponsorship in Arabic.

questions.q: What is the name of the Arab world's first nuclear power plant? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet identifies Barakah as the Arab world's first nuclear power plant.

questions.q: Which country, besides Qatar, shares the UAE's maritime border in the Persian Gulf? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the UAE's maritime borders in the Persian Gulf are with Qatar and Iran.

questions.q: Who is the UAE's Prime Minister? (full name)
accept: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum
questions.explanation: The booklet names Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum as Prime Minister.
